You are sourcing the BEST possible business ACQUISITIONS for Hooman across a specific category. This is an EXPLORATORY WIDE SEARCH (side quest), separate from his main research. Relaxed constraints:
  - Capital: up to ~$500K of HIS OWN CASH (all-cash within ~$500K; note if a good deal needs more via financing).
  - Time: RELAXED — he is willing to work harder or even QUIT HIS DAY JOB for the right business. So full-time,
    hands-on, owner-operated businesses are now IN SCOPE (not just passive/part-time).
  - Type: broaden beyond SaaS. Find the genuinely best deals in YOUR category.
  - Goal: the best acquisition available, full stop (strong cash flow, fair price, durable, improvable).

FOUNDER: Adobe eng manager (AI/ML, data engineering, cloud/infra, EE bachelor's, mech-eng friends, strong diligence/analytical ability). CRITICAL: he is a **CANADIAN CITIZEN, not a US person** — **SBA 7(a)/504 loans generally require a US citizen or permanent resident, so the standard US "10% down + SBA" leverage may NOT be available to him.** Assess financing realistically (all-cash within $500K, seller notes/vendor take-back, or Canadian options like BDC/bank) and FLAG when a deal only works with US-style leverage he may not qualify for.

YOUR CATEGORY: SaaS / software / apps
  Scope: Vertical B2B SaaS, micro-SaaS, established software, content/data products — but now up to ~$500K (bigger, stickier assets than the $300K search). Acquire.com, Empire Flippers, Flippa, FE International, Microns.

Read /home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/acquisitions_500k/README.md for the mandate. Do REAL WEB RESEARCH (WebSearch/WebFetch): browse the actual marketplaces/brokers for this category (BizBuySell, Acquire.com, Empire Flippers, Flippa, Quiet Light, BizQuest, franchise resale sites, etc.). Capture REAL current listings with real numbers — asking price, revenue, SDE/cash flow, multiple, age, location. Do NOT invent listings; mark gated fields "gated". Prioritize deals that fit ~$500K (all-cash or light seller-financing) with strong, durable cash flow.

WRITE your findings to /home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/acquisitions_500k/categories/saas_software.md (use Write; create folders; include listing URLs where public; cite sources). THEN return the structured schema. Be honest and quantified — for each category give the real economics (typical SDE multiple, cash yield, owner-hours) and an honest verdict on whether it's a strong vein for the best ~$500K buy.

# Category: SaaS / Software / Apps — Acquisitions @ ~$500K

**Researched**: 2026-07-03 by Claude (Opus 4.8). Owner: Hooman Shariati.
**Mandate**: `../README.md`. Wide search, up to ~$500K of Hooman's own cash, full-time
in scope, Canadian citizen (no SBA leverage assumed).

---

## 1. Category economics (real, from the marketplaces browsed)

Sources browsed 2026-07-03: BizBuySell (software & app category, pages 1–5),
Empire Flippers marketplace, BizQuest software category, FE International.

**Typical multiples in the $200K–$600K software band:**
- BizBuySell market context (self-reported medians): median software asking price
  **~$1.0M**, valuation averages **~2.06x revenue / ~3.60x earnings (SDE/EBITDA)**.
  Source: bizbuysell.com/software-and-app-companies-for-sale.
- The **sub-$600K** band skews to two very different animals:
  1. **Real vertical B2B SaaS with cash flow** — trades ~**2.5x–3.5x SDE** (e.g. EH&S
     compliance SaaS $325K on $110K SDE = **~3.0x**; email-service-provider SaaS $345K on
     $115.7K SDE = **~3.0x**).
  2. **App/AI "starter" listings** — either giveaway multiples on distressed/declining
     revenue (Intermittent Fasting app $200K on $166K EBITDA = 1.2x, a red flag not a
     bargain) or inflated multiples on tiny MRR (AI Assistant app $575K at 5.5x).
- **Empire Flippers / Acquire micro-SaaS**: content/subscription assets commonly at
  **~30–40x monthly profit (≈2.5x–3.3x annual)**; the one in-band SaaS on EF (#94153) was
  32x monthly BUT profit −50% YoY.

**Cash yield a ~$500K all-cash buy realistically produces:**
- At a fair ~3.0x SDE multiple, **$500K buys ~$165K SDE ≈ $13–14K/month** pre-tax owner
  cash flow, ~33% cash-on-cash — IF the revenue is stable. That is a strong yield vs any
  passive alternative and the whole reason software beats most categories on this metric.
- Caveat: SaaS SDE is only "real" if churn is low and the product isn't AI-commoditizable.
  Many sub-$600K "SaaS" listings are services dressed as SaaS or have declining revenue,
  which drops the *durable* yield well below the headline.

**Owner-hours**: Highly variable. True product SaaS with a support/dev contractor can run
**~10–25 hr/wk** (part-time viable). "SEO services / agency-with-software" listings that
dominate this price band are effectively **full-time service businesses (30–50 hr/wk)** —
recurring revenue but owner-and-labor-dependent, not passive.

---

## 2. Real current listings (browsed 2026-07-03; numbers as displayed, some fields gated)

Best-fit for a ~$500K all-cash buy with durable cash flow, best first.

### A. Environmental Compliance & SDS (EH&S) B2B Software — **TOP PICK**
- Source: BizBuySell software category (page 4).
- Location: Grand Rapids, MI. Asking **$325,000**. Cash flow (SDE) **$110,000**.
  Multiple **~3.0x SDE**. Age: gated ("established"). Revenue: gated.
- Vertical B2B SaaS in environmental, health & safety compliance / Safety Data Sheets.
  Recurring revenue, regulatory-mandate demand driver (SDS management is legally required
  under OSHA HazCom / GHS). Niche, sticky, sub-$500K all-cash.
- Fits ~$500K all-cash with **~$175K left over** for a support/dev contractor + working
  capital. Strongest founder-fit + durability combo in the band.

### B. Email Service Provider SaaS (17-year-old, 425 customers)
- Source: BizBuySell software category (page 4).
- Location: California. Asking **$345,000**. Cash flow **$115,753**. Multiple **~3.0x**.
  Age **17 years**. **425 paying customers**, **88% gross margin**.
- Durable, long-lived, high-margin, diversified customer base (no single-customer
  concentration). Risk: email infra is a mature/competitive space; growth likely flat and
  deliverability/anti-spam ops are a real operational tax.

### C. "Unique Tech Services, Software, and AI Company"
- Source: BizBuySell software category (page 2).
- Location: Hillsborough County, FL. Asking **$650,000**. Cash flow **$210,000**.
  Multiple **~3.1x**. Age: gated. Revenue: gated. Scalable product line + established base.
- **OVER-500K** all-cash but the best SDE in the band; would need ~$150K seller note or
  price negotiation to fit. "Services + software + AI" wording suggests meaningful service
  labor (owner-dependent) — diligence needed to separate SaaS ARR from consulting.

### D. Healthcare Documentation / Clinical-Workflow Software
- Source: BizBuySell software category (page 3).
- Location: Alpharetta, GA. Asking **$500,000**. Cash flow: gated. Revenue: gated.
  "Long-established niche platform serving treating-provider practices."
- Fits $500K all-cash exactly (no room for buffer). Sticky vertical, but healthcare =
  HIPAA + slow sales + integration burden; cash flow undisclosed is a diligence gate.

### E. Healthcare Software Portfolio (3 platforms: hospice / home health / residential)
- Source: BizBuySell software category (page 3).
- Location: Glendale, CA. Asking **$500,000**. Cash flow: gated. Revenue: gated.
- Three products = diversification but also 3x the maintenance surface for a solo owner.
  Compliance-heavy vertical.

### F. Business/Finance Reimbursement-Audit SaaS — #94153 (Empire Flippers)
- Source: empireflippers.com/marketplace listing **#94153**.
- Asking **$377,472**. Monthly net profit **$11,797** (SDE ~$141.6K/yr). Monthly revenue
  **$31,728**. Multiple **32x monthly (~2.7x annual)**. Founded 2021 (5 yrs).
  Monetization "Service, SaaS".
- **RED FLAG**: profit **−50% YoY**, revenue **−37% YoY**. Declining — the low-ish
  multiple is a discount for decline, not a bargain. Pass unless the decline has a fixable,
  diligence-verifiable cause.

### G. AI Fundraising SaaS (nonprofits)
- Source: BizQuest / BizBuySell. Texas. Asking **$350,000**. Cash flow **$18,608**.
  Multiple **~18.8x SDE** (very high). 77% recurring revenue on non-cancellable contracts.
- **Overpriced on current cash flow** — priced on ARR/growth story, not SDE. Pass at ask.

### H. AI Assistant App w/ $16K MRR
- Source: BizBuySell (page 5). Nashua, NH. Asking **$575,000**. EBITDA **$103,814**.
  Multiple **5.54x**. Consumer/prosumer AI productivity app.
- **OVER-500K** and, more importantly, a **consumer AI wrapper** — highly AI-commoditizable
  (model providers can subsume the feature). High multiple + high obsolescence risk. Pass.

### Reference / context listings (not buys)
- AI-Automated Digital Services Agency — Sheridan, WY. **$985,000**, revenue $580K, SDE
  **$328K TTM**, 57% margin, 43 profitable months (BizQuest). Great business, over budget.
- Translation/Localization company — Worldwide, $750K, SDE $170K (BizBuySell). Service biz.
- AI Support Translation Tool — Delaware, $750K, SDE $229.8K, 120+ languages (BizBuySell).

---

## 3. Financing reality for a CANADIAN citizen (no SBA)

**The core constraint holds.** SBA 7(a)/504 program rules (SBA SOP 50 10) require the
operating business to be at least 51% owned by US citizens or lawful permanent residents
(green-card holders). A **Canadian citizen with no US permanent residency generally cannot
use standard SBA leverage** to buy a US business. (SBA does allow certain "Legal Permanent
Resident" / conditional structures, but not a non-resident foreign national.) The classic
US "10% down, SBA covers the rest" playbook is **off the table** unless Hooman first
obtains LPR status. Verify his exact status before assuming any US-loan path.

**What this means per deal:**
- The listings above are almost all **US-based**, so US buyer-financing (SBA, most US bank
  acquisition lines) is likely unavailable to him.
- **All-cash within ~$500K is the reliable path.** Listings A ($325K), B ($345K), F
  ($377K) fit all-cash with buffer; D/E ($500K) fit all-cash with no buffer.
- **Seller note / vendor take-back** is the most realistic leverage: on software deals a
  10–30% seller note (paid from the business's own cash flow) is common and does NOT
  require citizenship. Prioritize sellers open to a note — it also aligns their incentives.
- **Canadian options (BDC, Canadian banks)** finance acquisitions but strongly prefer the
  *target* to be Canadian-domiciled with Canadian cash flow; they are a poor fit for buying
  a US software company. Realistically not a lever for these US listings.
- **Net**: treat every deal here as an **all-cash-or-seller-note** decision. Flagged per
  listing above (all in-band ones are FITS-ALL-CASH except C and H which are OVER-500K).

---

## 4. Hooman-fit

Strong on paper — this is the category his skills map to most directly.
- **Where his edge is real**: (1) **Diligence alpha** — he can read code, assess
  churn/cohort data, spot AI-commoditization risk, and evaluate infra cost/scalability
  better than a typical searcher. (2) **Value creation** — for a stagnant vertical SaaS
  (e.g. the EH&S/SDS or email-provider assets), he can modernize the stack, add AI
  features, cut infra cost, and re-accelerate growth. That is exactly the "improvable
  durable asset" the mandate wants.
- **Where his edge is irrelevant / a trap**: the sub-$600K band is heavy with **SEO/agency
  "recurring revenue"** businesses that are really full-time service shops — his technical
  edge doesn't help and the owner-dependence is high. And **consumer AI-wrapper apps** are
  precisely where his own knowledge tells him the moat is thin (model providers eat the
  feature). He should filter those out.
- **Time**: he's willing to go full-time, which unlocks the owner-operated vertical-SaaS
  deals here. But the best-fit ones (A, B) are runnable ~part-time with one contractor,
  leaving room to build/improve rather than just operate.

---

## 5. Category verdict

**This is a STRONG vein — arguably the strongest category for Hooman specifically** —
because it maximizes his two edges (technical diligence + value creation) and produces the
best cash yield per dollar (fair deals ~3x SDE → ~33% cash-on-cash all-cash). It fits the
all-cash-only Canadian financing reality well: real, durable, sub-$500K vertical B2B SaaS
exists at ~3x SDE and can be bought outright with cash to spare.

**Best sub-play: bootstrapped, boring, regulation-adjacent VERTICAL B2B SaaS at ~3x SDE**
— e.g. the EH&S/SDS compliance software ($325K / $110K SDE / ~3.0x) or the 17-year email
provider ($345K / $115.7K SDE / 88% margin). Sticky recurring revenue, mandate-driven
demand, diversified customers, priced fairly, all-cash-affordable with buffer, and directly
improvable by an AI/infra engineer.

**Avoid within the category**: consumer AI-wrapper apps (commoditization), "SaaS" listings
that are service/SEO agencies (owner-labor-dependent, no tech edge), declining-revenue
assets priced at a "discount" (#94153, −50% YoY), and ARR-priced growth stories at 15–20x
SDE (AI Fundraising SaaS) where you pay for a future that may not arrive.

**Diligence must-dos before any offer**: verify gated cash flow, pull cohort/churn data,
confirm no single-customer concentration, assess AI-commoditization risk of the core
feature, and confirm the deal works **all-cash or with a seller note** (no SBA).
